observations: Three photos show a black, rectangular device with a circular lens on one end and a textured side with a small circular button or port on the other.
The device has a glossy finish with visible smudges and fingerprints, especially on the top surface.
A coiled black cable with a USB connector is attached and tied with a green rubber band.
The device is placed on a white surface with a watermark 'McSteve POSTED ON JIJI' and contact details.
No visible branding or model text is readable on the device itself in any photo.
The seller claims it is a 'Microsoft Xbox One Motion Sensing Kinetic Camera'.

claims.claim: This is a Neatly used Microsoft Xbox One Motion Sensing Kinetic Camera And it Works with Xbox One
claims.evidence: No photo shows this clearly enough to read.

risks.proof: A video showing the device connected to a Xbox One and in motion, or a screenshot of the Kinect interface in use.

risks.risk: The device may be a counterfeit or non-genuine product.
risks.proof: A close-up of the device's serial number or a photo of the original packaging with branding.

risks.risk: The cable may be damaged or non-functional.
risks.proof: A close-up of the USB connector and a video showing the cable connecting to a device.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cable may be faulty

proof_requests: A close-up photo of the device's serial number or any label.
A video showing the device connected to a Xbox One and in motion.
A close-up of the USB cable connector and a video showing it connecting to a device.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
